mission: Encode is a small youth-founded advocacy team that writes and lobbies for AI safety laws, builds unusual coalitions (parents, conservatives, safety researchers, artists) and influences leaders. It describes itself as 'pro-human pro-AI' and refuses money from corporations, foreign governments and frontier-AI executives.

key_work.title: California SB 53 (signed 2025)
key_work.plain_summary: Encode co-sponsored California's frontier-AI law requiring the biggest AI companies to publish safety frameworks, report critical incidents and protect whistleblowers.

key_work.title: Opposing the federal AI 'moratorium' on state laws
key_work.plain_summary: Encode organised a coalition against a proposal to stop US states from regulating AI; the provision was later struck down in the Senate.

status_note: founded July 2020 as Encode Justice by Sneha Revanur; now operates as Encode / Encode AI (rename date not published)
status_raw: renamed — founded July 2020 as Encode Justice by Sneha Revanur; now operates as Encode / Encode AI (rename date not published)
funding_note: Funded by individual donors and foundations (e.g. Heising-Simons, Survival and Flourishing Fund, Future of Life Institute); refuses corporate, foreign-government and frontier-AI-executive money (Who we are page).

warnings.text: AI could enable bioweapons, hurt children, erode individual liberty and even escape human control.
Well-funded anti-regulation lobbying and super PACs try to block safety rules.
Federal pre-emption of state AI laws would remove the main safeguards currently being passed.

recommendations.text: Pass state and federal laws requiring frontier-AI transparency, incident reporting and independent audits.
Keep states' power to regulate AI (oppose blanket federal pre-emption).
